To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a combination of radioscintigraphy, lymphoscintigraphy, and blue dye injection for sentinel lymph node biopsy is safe and effective for the staging of patients with squamous-cell carcinoma of the penis, (2) this approach is superior to the use of blue dye alone, and (3) it is associated with a low incidence of false-negative results and a low rate of complications.

(i) the use of the dynamic sentinel lymph node procedure is a reliable method to identify the first echelon nodes in patients with penile cancer and palpable ingunal lymph nodes; (ii) the procedure can be performed with minimal morbidity, and (iii) it can be used as an alternative to inguinal lymphadenectomy in patients with peni cancer and clinically positive inguinal nodes.
the use of the sentinel node concept is a reliable method for the detection of metastases in the inguinal region of patients with squamous carcinoma of the penis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of dynamic sentinel lymph-node biopsy in patients with palpable inguional nodes in patients with squamos cell carcinoma of the penile.
the development of a new method for evaluating the dynamic sentinel lymph node (DSLN) biopsy in patients with palpable inguinally metastatic SCC of the penis.
the development of a new technique of dynamic sentinel lymph-node biopsy (DSLNB), which is a minimally invasive technique for the diagnosis of lymph node metastases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is insufficient to support or refute the use of sentinel lymph node biopsy for the treatment of patients with penile carcinoma.

dynamic sentinel lymph node mapping and biopsy is a reliable technique for staging of clinically palpable inguional lymph nodes in patients with penile cancer, and should be considered the standard of care.

dynamic sentinel lymph node (SLN) biopsy is a reliable procedure for the staging of patients with squamous carcinoma of the penis with clinically palpable inguional nodes, but the procedure has not been validated in patients with clinically impalpale nodes.

we are able to show the importance of the role of the lymphatic system in cancer metastasis and the importance of the lymphatic vessels in cancer treatment.
we have demonstrated that the dynamic sentinel lymph node (DSLN) biopsy is an effective method for staging patients with squamous carcinoma of the penis.
we have shown the feasibility and safety of the technique in patients with SCC of the penile cancer with clinically palpable lymph nodes.

the use of a combination of blue and green dyes in DSLNB is safe, effective, and reliable for mapping the SLN.
the use of dynamic sentinel lymphadenectomy (DSL) in the management of patients with penile cancer and inguinal lymphadenopathy is safe and effective.
